messages:
cheng: heads-up, we've been seeing occasional 99.9 spikes from the global continuous-batcher; noisy tenants seem to create long-tail queues. thinking about splitting into small tenant islands to isolate noise.
maya: interested. islanding should help p99 but terrified of KV cache fragmentation / warmup. any data? :thinking_face:
evan: ran a micro-experiment: 8 tenant-islands by shard. throughput -3% but p95 improved 15% and p99 improved ~30%.
lia: where does the warmup penalty show up? is it per-request or per-batch?
evan: per-cold-batch. median warmup ~70ms, occasional >200ms until local KV warms. total p99 reduced because islanding prevented cross-tenant interference.
maya: hybrid idea: keep a global pool for low-priority/bulk tenants and small islands for top 15-25% latency-sensitive ones. admission routes by tenant priority + short traffic fingerprint.
cheng: sketch config (proto):
```
islands:
  - name: hot_small
    selector: tenant_priority>=8
    max_slots: 0.2 * gpu_slots
    borrowable: true
    borrow_policy: proportional_recent_rps
global:
  max_slots: remaining
  eviction: kv-prefix-stream-to-shared-warm_cache
```
lia: eviction is crucial. if we evict naive LRU we pay huge recompute. propose streaming hot prefixes to a shared warm cache before eviction.
maya: agree. also need per-island metrics: kv_hit_ratio_1m, cold_batch_latency_1m, and an alert if cold_batch_latency > 100ms for 3 consecutive windows.
cheng: headroom accounting is another must: islands should be allowed to borrow but repay. propose a simple ledger: islands get reserved headroom credits, can borrow from global up to X, repay asynchronously as traffic stabilizes. failure mode: borrow saturates global -> degrade islands LIFO.
evan: canary status: ops-bot kicked off continuous-batcher/hybrid-islands v0.3 on 3 nodes. can we get traces?
ops-bot: deploy-batcher-canary: continuous-batcher/hybrid-islands v0.3 canary rollout started on 3 machines; traces available at /infra/batcher/canary/1793334501 after ingestion (~5m).
maya: good. i'll run a 50k-trace sim (real traffic replay) comparing global-only vs islanded vs hybrid. metrics: p50/p95/p99/p99.9, cost delta (GPU-min), and KV recompute ops.
lia: i'll prototype a tiny shared warm cache (LRU with size tuning) that islands can spill hot prefixes into. measure mem overhead vs warmup savings.
evan: i'll add per-island instrumentation for kv_hit_ratio and cold_batch_latency to the canary build.
cheng: risks to call out: 1) GPU memory blowup due to replicated KV, 2) island hoarding leading to global starvation, 3) complexity in rollback during rollout. mitigation: quantized KV (lower precision), headroom ledger + borrow caps, controlled canary rollout with automatic fallback.
maya: acceptance criteria for next step: hybrid must reduce p99.9 by X% (TBD) with <5% cost increase in predicted GPU-min. otherwise iterate.
cheng: timeline: sim results Wed, headroom prototype Thu, RFC update Fri EOD. tagging @maya @evan @lia for visibility.
maya: starting sim now, will drop numbers in this thread.
evan: instrumented canary -> will post preliminary warmup graphs.
lia: shared-warm-cache proto ready locally, will deploy to canary once we have metrics.
cheng: thanks all. if sim shows hybrid wins on tail at acceptable cost, we'll follow phased rollout with gradual island count increase. :rocket:
